text.p: NARODNA OBRODA - The development of the Slovak crown will closely depend on whether the government succeeds in implementing measures aimed at improving the trade balance, analysts said.
- Only 4,809 privatisation bonds were matched in anonymous trading since the beginning of this year, compared with some 130,000 bonds traded through direct deals.
- President Michal Kovac on Tuesday visits Poland where he will join other central Europe presidents to attend a mass by Pope John Paul.

- Tatra Kupon a.s., an investment fund created for the voucher privatisation scheme, will pay a dividend of 166 crowns per share from a 1996 after-tax profit of 21.93 million crowns. The fund's net profit per share was 184.90 crowns.
- Money market dealers say the crown liquidity shortage resulting from the central bank's fight for a stable currency can soon threaten banks' ability to pay clients.
appointed a successor for Foreign Minister Pavol Hamzik who resigned on May 26. President Kovac said he was considering using his constitutional right to name the minister.
- The eight strongest opposition parties and the opposition Party of the Democratic Left (SDL) said they would continue in preparations of one draft law on direct presidential elections.

- Opposition parties have called protest meetings in several towns and cities around the country on Tuesday to demonstrate against the government's thwarting of the two referendums on NATO membership and direct presidential elections.
- Trade unions of the Bratislava public transport company on Tuesday begin an indefinite strike to protest against social and working conditions.

PRAVDA - Jan Drgonec, a member of the Slovak Constitutional Court, said the failed NATO and presidential elections plebiscites should have been carried out with the question on direct presidential elections.
HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - Some regional branches of several Slovak banks stopped exchanging crowns for hard curencies due to an accute crown and foreign exchange liquidity shortage on local money markets.

- The Slovak government is expected to discuss at its regular Tuesday session an issuance of state bonds to cover housing construction later this year. No other major economic items are on the session's preliminary agenda.
